Who, and what they adopted
plantation managers and operators on palm oil and tea estates; 'several large plantation companies' (unnamed)Precision agronomy: drones with multispectral imaging, soil and weather sensors (moisture, temperature, light, pH), satellite data; ML recommends fertilisation and irrigation
Problem
land-management inefficiency reduces yield; climate uncertainty
Technology
drones, multispectral imaging, soil/weather sensors, satellite data, ML recommendations, automated irrigation
Outcome
AI image processing 10,000 ha in 4 h vs 14+ days for 20 people (company's own figure, reported by Bloomberg); no yield figures
How to adopt
Have estate maps and a drone pilot or contracted drone service; start with one block and compare imagery readings with agronomist checks; expect ongoing flight, data-processing and agronomy staffing.
Risks
Recommendation accuracy unproven without yield data; dependence on drone or analytics vendors; skills gaps on estates.
